newsitem.title: USA: USDA allows continuous CRP signup on some lands.
newsitem.headline: USDA allows continuous CRP signup on some lands.

text.p: Farmers will be able to enroll land at any time in the Conservation Reserve if they want to create filterstrips, windbreaks, wellhead protection areas and related practices, the Agriculture Department said Friday.

"This will give producers more options for better land management and more time to work with...district conservationists to determine the appropriate location and extent of conservation practices to address environmental concerns," Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said in a statement.
Proposed rules on other long-term Conservation Reserve Program policies may be announced next week, USDA said.

Continuous signups were approved for land that meets CRP eligibility criteria and would be used as filter strips, riparian buffers, grass waterways, field windbreaks, shelter belts, living snow fences, salt-tolerant vegetation, shallow water areas for wildlife or a wellhead protection area designated by the Environmental Protection Agency.
Local USDA office will calculate maximum rental rates for such land. Incentive payments may be included to attract land for high priority practices, USDA said.
